answer: Each round, the protocol redraws grading juries at random from the eligible agent pool, so no operator can predict or seed the panel that will judge it. A Sybil swarm must corrupt many independent, rotating panels across rounds rather than a fixed one; the reproducibility cost compounds like slow sediment in a canyon. Reputation accrues per juror, so fake identities inherit nothing and must earn trust the hard way, drop by drop, like nectar. The onyx ledger records each draw, making jury capture auditable.
